records.mutation: replace parametrization warning with the n-th-root-of-c trap and an original-equation verification
records.subagent_summary: All 8 rollouts terminated normally (finish_reason stop, 3.4k-7.8k tokens), so budget is not the issue; 7 of 8 were correct and every rollout visibly followed the incumbent's take-moduli-then-complete-the-square recipe. The single failure came from taking the modulus without extracting the n-th root of the constant, which produced a self-consistent-but-wrong circle that survived its own internal check and even the incumbent's suggested substitution check, because the derived equation was verified rather than the original. I therefore cut the dead-weight clause warning against a parametrization no rollout used, and spent those tokens on an explicit k^n = |c| sanity check plus a verification anchored to the original equation.

The failure is pure non-termination from endless re-verification ('Wait' appears 34-71 times per rollout, and the incumbent's 'otherwise minimize over the symmetry-reduced range' plus 'confirm it by pairing congruent pieces' invited an open-ended angle scan), not bad geometry, so I removed the extra confirmation branch and replaced it with an explicit two-sample-then-stop rule plus an immediate-box and three-line-write-up cap.

records.mutation: replace discriminant-panic loop with a bounded one-flip repair rule
records.subagent_summary: All 4 of 8 failures were finish_reason=length at the full 16384-token cap, and every one of them hit a negative discriminant, then spent thousands of tokens re-verifying identical algebra and restarting with renamed variables instead of correcting the sign of the displacement; the 4 successes reached the same quadratic with the offset oriented the right way and finished in 8-12k tokens. The incumbent already said "do not restart" but gave no bounded repair action, so the revision names the exact fix (negate the displacement, redo only the cross-multiplication), caps it at one flip, and states the base-c<1 direction explicitly as the concrete first move.

records.mutation: replace abstract state-graph DP with explicit push/pop stack encoding, the two observed traps, and a one-value stopping rule stated without answer-marker language
records.subagent_summary: All 8 fresh rollouts scored 0 under the incumbent state-graph/DP hint and none actually built that state graph: 4 declared the resulting order forced (probability 1), 3 treated it as uniform over 4!, and 1 blew the 16384-token cap enumerating sequences ad hoc. So the revision names the concrete push/pop stack encoding and the per-step 1/2-versus-forced weighting as the opening move, explicitly negates the two observed traps, and closes with a commit-to-one-value-and-stop rule, since the one rollout that did reach the correct value lost reward by continuing on to emit a second marked result for the later part.

records.mutation: replace abstract functional language with an executable test-polynomial first move plus anti-looping rule
records.subagent_summary: All 8 rollouts scored 0 and 7 of 8 terminated by hitting the 16384-token cap with no boxed answer; the incumbent's abstract 'linear functional / vanishing moments' framing gave no executable first step, so the student repeatedly conflated the weights a_i with coefficients of a polynomial in x, declared the system inconsistent, and looped through tiny n=2,3,4 cases guessing patterns. The revision names the exact misreading to avoid, gives the concrete first move (weight the equations by c_k to build a test polynomial and evaluate at the nodes), specifies choosing f to vanish at 0 and at all other nodes so one weight survives, and adds an explicit do-not-restart-and-box-early rule to fix the non-termination that dominated the failures.

records.mutation: generalize divisor-count technique and add anti-relitigation / single-pass markup rules
records.subagent_summary: Fresh training run scored 8/8 with no truncation, so the incumbent is already on-task and the remaining cost is wasted reasoning, not error: the longest rollouts burned thousands of tokens oscillating between the aggregate and per-unit readings of the same figures, and several recomputed the markup twice (before and after dividing) to confirm the identical result. The revision drops problem-specific scaffolding (street layout, the interpretation label) in favour of a reusable rule set - resolve aggregate-vs-per-unit once, convert integrality into a divides/gcd condition, take the largest admissible count without enumerating divisors, apply the markup as one (1+p) multiplication - which should preserve on-task accuracy while transferring to any integrality-pinned counting problem.

records.mutation: replace abstract affine framing with executable degree-reduction first move plus anti-looping commit rule
records.subagent_summary: All 5 failing rollouts ended with finish_reason=length at the 16384-token cap and no boxed answer; every one of them had accepted the affine link q=a*p+b but then either tried to match coefficients of the degree-9 composition or blindly guessed constants, and two burned thousands of tokens re-deriving the leading-term condition after an earlier arithmetic slip. The 3 successful rollouts all shared one move the incumbent hint never named: substituting u=p(x) to reduce the identity to a single-variable equation, ruling out the a=+1 branch quickly, and letting the leftover cubic coefficient cancel. The revision therefore trades the incumbent's abstract 'reduces to commuting with an affine involution' language for that concrete degree-reduction step, a one-line branch test, and an explicit box-and-never-restart rule targeting the observed non-termination.

records.mutation: replace abstract 'compose into bitwise affine permutation' with concrete explicit-list first move, ban piecewise patching, add commit-and-box rule
records.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts scored 3/8: four of five failures hit the 16384-token cap (finish_reason=length) after producing mutually inconsistent hand traces for small sizes and then oscillating between several candidate closed forms, and the one terminating failure trusted a sloppy small-case trace over verification. The incumbent named the destination (bitwise affine permutation, cycle structure, minimality proof) but no executable first move, so the revision front-loads an explicit position-list trace of a couple of small sizes plus orbit tracking, uses the bit-string map only as a cross-check, and adds the observed-failure guard: a disagreement between sizes means the trace is wrong rather than the answer being piecewise, plus an explicit stop-exploring-and-box rule to fight non-termination.
